issues.body: On the incremental branch, `extract_added` mutates `self.ex.names` and `resaturate` grows the saturation, but nothing updates `self.ex.report.named_classes`. The later assignment `report.report = self.ex.report` therefore only copies the pre-edit count. This contradicts the public `IncrementalReport::report` documentation, which says `named_classes` reports the live concept-index size, and `hierarchy()` propagates the same stale report. The differential helper explicitly excludes `named_classes`, so the tests cannot catch the defect. A fresh restriction-node edit is a direct witness: it mints normalization concepts while the reported count remains unchanged.
issues.fix_hint: After delta extraction/resaturation, set `self.ex.report.named_classes` from the current live name table (using the same count semantics as full extraction), before constructing either report/hierarchy. Extend the fresh-restriction incremental test to assert the documented live count and, where appropriate, distinguish it from a from-scratch count only because historical fresh names are retained.
issues.title: Incremental edits leave Report::named_classes stale

verdict.summary: The incremental saturation path is backed by meaningful full-reclassification differentials, but the new public reporting contract is not implemented: after an incremental edit that mints concepts, `Report::named_classes` remains the value captured at initial extraction. The code and docs explicitly promise that it reflects the live concept-index size, while the tests deliberately omit this field. This makes the returned `IncrementalReport` and `ClassHierarchy` observably stale even when the hierarchy itself is correct.
